## Goal (user story)

As a developer/QA, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode (extending MainStreetMonteCarlo) that runs ≥200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics, so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.

## Context

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. Architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner), but the harness validates the head-to-head (human vs 1 AI) path initially; N>2 extension is a future parameterisation.

## Scope

- Head-to-head harness extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (new entry point or flag): both players act per shared-day, same seed → deterministic head-to-head run.
- ≥200 seeds; outputs win/score distributions plus per-player metrics (wins per owner, average score per owner, draw/early-end handling).
- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).
- Endless continuation (deferred).
- N>2 Monte Carlo — harness is N-player-extensible (numOpponents param) but AC4 validates head-to-head; broader N is a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Head-to-head harness runs ≥200 seeds with deterministic head-to-head execution (same seed → same per-owner outcome) and produces win/score distributions (win rate per owner, median/average score per owner).
- [ ] **AC2:** Per-player metrics include at least wins, average score, and loss-reason distribution per owner plus a deterministic summary (draw/early-end handling documented).
- [ ] **AC3:** Extension of `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (not a replacement); existing `runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` and `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC4:** Validated against the adapted competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness extension (win/score distributions, per-player metrics).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive Monte Carlo tests (determinism, distributions, guardrails).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model + phase machine + income routing + AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038)
- Architecture: N-player-ready state/phase; harness parametrises head-to-head initially
data.title: Competitive Monte Carlo harness: head-to-head simulation

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the shared street rendered with owner-coloured slots, shared-market phase alternation, and SFX/animations (per AGENTS.md §8), so competitive ownership is visually and audibly unambiguous.

## Context

AC5 of the parent epic is engine-only: no game-selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome. This planning-created child (per AC5 “deferred to a planning child” and producer Q2 “planning”) captures the deferred rendering scope for the next milestone. Worker must use core-engine animation helpers with `soundManager` + `sfx` (AGENTS.md §8: every animated action needs sound + animation; SFX keys via `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, no literals).

## Scope

- Competitive scene (Phaser scene) with SLL layout.
- Owner-coloured street: each placed business's street slot tinted by owner (e.g. player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is immediately readable.
- Shared-market phase alternation: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day with visible whose-turn affordance.
- SFX/animations for all competitive actions (deal/flip/place/discard/illegal) via helpers + `SoundManager`, respecting reduced-motion and mute.
- Turn alternation SFX/animation sequencing so AI actions are visible (delayed AI turn like Coloretto precedent).

## Out of scope

- Engine state/phase/income/AI/Monte Carlo (parent epic siblings).
- Game-selector entry — include only when the scene is ready for play (within this child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Competitive scene renders the shared street with per-slot owner colour (player vs AI unambiguously distinct); SLL layout used (no hardcoded pixel positions).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared-market phase alternation is visible (whose turn) and input is gated to the active player; AI turn is animated with a brief delay.
- [ ] **AC3:** Every competitive action that uses a core-engine animation helper is wired with SFX (via helper `soundManager`/`sfx` params or `GameEventEmitter`/`SoundManager`); SFX keys follow `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention; reduced-motion and mute respected.
- [ ] **AC4:** Build + unit tests pass; smoke browser coverage for the scene.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScene.ts` — Competitive scene (owner-coloured street, phase alternation, SFX).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveRenderer.ts` — Owner-colour helpers (tinting by ownerId).
- `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` source of truth for SFX keys.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-scene.browser.test.ts` — Smoke/browser coverage.

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode (engine-only; rendering deferred here per AC5)
- Siblings: state, phase, income/events, AI strategy, Monte Carlo (engine foundation this child renders)

# Intake Draft: Tutorial confuses time duration of turn (CG-0MTMYIHKO001QCWL)

## Problem statement

Main Street treats one turn as one week of in-game time (the annual calendar
advances one week per turn and the HUD shows `Week W · Year Y`), but the
tutorial, several in-game messages, and much of the documentation still
describe a turn as a "day" and speak of "today"/"tomorrow"/"overnight". This
contradicts itself inside the tutorial itself (it says both "this week" and
"tomorrow" for the same span) and confuses players about how long a turn is.
All documentation, all user-facing text, and the internal "day"-themed
identifiers must be standardised on **one turn = one week**.

## Users

- **Players** — must see one consistent time model: a turn is a week; the
  tutorial and in-game prompts should never call it a day.
- **Designers / writers / localisers** — need a single canonical vocabulary
  ("turn", "week", "this week", "next week", "Turn N") for future content.
- **Engine consumers (save/load, transcript, replay, Monte Carlo, tests)** —
  must keep loading old runs and replaying deterministically across the
  identifier rename.

User stories:

- As a player, I want the tutorial to describe the turn I am about to end as
  a week, not a day, so I understand that ending the turn advances a week.
- As a writer, I want one documented vocabulary rule so I do not reintroduce
  "today"/"tomorrow" in new tutorial or UI text.
- As a returning player, I want my existing save to keep working after the
  terminology change so I do not lose a run.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Canonical vocabulary is documented** — a short terminology section in
   `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (cross-referenced from
   `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md`) states: one turn = one week;
   in-world time is written as "week"/"this week"/"next week"; the activity-log
   header remains `Turn N`; "day"/"today"/"tomorrow"/"overnight" must not be
   used as turn synonyms. *(Verification: doc review + the guard check in AC 5.)*
2. **Tutorial and all user-facing in-game text standardised** —
   `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` and every user-facing string
   (HUD tooltips, instruction text, legality reasons, activity-log text) use
   week terminology; no user-facing string contains a forbidden token.
   *(Verification: forbidden-token check + existing tutorial/UI unit and browser
   tests pass.)*
3. **Internal day-themed identifiers and comments renamed** — `DayPhase` →
   `TurnPhase`, phase value `'DayStart'` → `'WeekStart'`, `executeDayStart` →
   `executeWeekStart`, `executeCompetitiveDayStart` →
   `executeCompetitiveWeekStart`, `animateDayBanner` → `animateWeekBanner`
   (param `day` → `turn`), local `advanceDay` → `advanceTurn`,
   `dayStartCoins`/`dayStartRep`/`dayStartScore` → `weekStartCoins`/`weekStartRep`/
   `weekStartScore`, plus the day-themed module/test/comment names; `state.turn`
   is retained as the canonical counter. *(Verification: `npm run build` + no
   references to the old symbols.)*
4. **Save and transcript compatibility preserved** — existing saves and
   campaign saves still deserialize after the rename. `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION`
   and `MAIN_STREET_CAMPAIGN_SCHEMA_VERSION` are bumped and a migration maps the
   old `'DayStart'` phase and `dayStart*` fields to the new names; a unit test
   round-trips a pre-change save. *(Verification: migration round-trip unit test.)*
5. **Every documentation occurrence updated** — all "day-as-turn" wording is
   replaced across **all** docs (living and historical), including
   `docs/main-street/*.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `example-games/main-street/README.md`,
   and `example-games/main-street/scenes/README.md`. A guard test/script asserts
   the source and docs contain no forbidden day-as-turn tokens. *(Verification:
   guard check + doc review.)*
6. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (release-gate
   only; during implementation run unit tests, `npm run test:dev` before audit).

## Constraints

- **No gameplay change.** This is a terminology/identifier refactor plus a save
  migration; economy, adjacency, incidents, and scoring behaviour must be
  unchanged. Determinism (seeded RNG, transcripts) must be preserved.
- **Keep the canonical labels already in use:** activity-log `Turn N` and HUD
  `Week W · Year Y` stay as-is.
- **Do not rename `state.turn`.** "Turn" is the canonical unit noun; a turn is
  one week. Only "day"-themed synonyms are renamed.
- **Backward compatibility is mandatory** for saves and campaign saves.
- **Doc-update policy:** documentation changes ship in the same commit as the
  rename (project AGENTS.md).
- **Surgical changes:** touch only what the terminology change requires; do not
  reword unrelated prose in historical docs beyond the day→week substitution.

## Existing state

- The calendar model (CG-0MTT0K9RX0004QTE) established one week per turn:
  `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` ("The calendar model advances one week per
  turn"), `state.week` / `state.year`, and the `advanceWeek()` helper
  (`MainStreetStateSetup.ts`). Every turn increments `state.turn` and calls
  `advanceWeek()` (`MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`).
- The HUD/banner already render `Week W · Year Y` (`scenes/MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts`),
  and the Help panel "Turn Flow" already says "Each turn is one week", "1 action
  per week", and "same-week move + play/place" (`scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`).
- The tutorial and several docs/messages still use the old day model:
  `i18n/tutorial-en.ts`, `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
  ("Each turn represents a day (or night) cycle."), plus HUD/instruction strings
  in `scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`, `MainStreetFormatting.ts`,
  `MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`, `MainStreetMarketSell.ts`,
  `MainStreetEngineActions.ts`, `scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`,
  and `MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`.
- `docs/main-street/tutorial-localization.md` already states the rule
  "turns not days", but the shipped tutorial text does not follow it.
- Day-themed identifier surface: ~116 references across `DayStart` (48),
  `executeDayStart` (17), `dayStartRep`/`dayStartCoins`/`dayStartScore` (34),
  `animateDayBanner` (8), `advanceDay` (7), `DayPhase` (7),
  `executeCompetitiveDayStart` (5); ~45 test files reference `'DayStart'`.

## Desired change

Apply the canonical vocabulary **everywhere** (producer decision: Q1=c,
Q2=everywhere):

1. **Tutorial + user-facing text** — rewrite tutorial strings and every
   in-game message so in-world time reads as weeks: "today"/"this day" →
   "this week"; "tomorrow"/"next day"/"start the new day" → "next week";
   "overnight" → "until next week"; "same-day" → "same-week". Keep the
   activity-log `Turn N` and HUD `Week W · Year Y`.
2. **Code identifiers + comments** — rename the day-themed identifiers listed
   in AC 3, update code comments accordingly, and rename the affected
   module/test files (e.g. `MainStreetEngineDayStart.ts` →
   `MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`, `day-banner*.test.ts` → `week-banner*.test.ts`).
3. **Persistence** — rename the serialised `'DayStart'` phase and `dayStart*`
   fields via a schema-version bump and migration so old saves still load.
4. **Documentation** — replace every day-as-turn occurrence in every doc,
   including historical snapshots (producer decision Q2=everywhere), while
   keeping non-turn uses of the word "day" untouched (e.g. the `Day Spa`
   business, the `Rainy Day`, `Volunteer Day`, `Farmers Market Day`,
   `St Brigid's Day`, and `May Day / Bealtaine` events).
5. **Guard rail** — add an automated forbidden-token check over user-facing
   string sources and docs so the vocabulary cannot regress.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/i18n/tutorial-en.ts` — Rewrite all tutorial
  strings to week terminology.
- `example-games/main-street/TutorialFlow.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/TutorialScenario.ts` — Update step comments/day map.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Rename `DayPhase` →
  `TurnPhase`, `'DayStart'` → `'WeekStart'`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineDayStart.ts` — Rename module and
  `executeDayStart` → `executeWeekStart`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — Rename
  `executeCompetitiveDayStart`, `'DayStart'` references.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `'DayStart'`
  references and day comments.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Export/alias updates.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — Rename serialised
  `dayStart*` fields; bump schema versions; add migration.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts` — Rename
  `animateDayBanner`, param `day` → `turn`.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` —
  Rename local `advanceDay`.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineActions.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`,
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — User-facing
  day wording → week wording.
- `docs/main-street/*.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`,
  `example-games/main-street/README.md`,
  `example-games/main-street/scenes/README.md` — Terminology updates.
- `tests/main-street/*` — Update renamed symbols and `'DayStart'` literals;
  add a save-migration round-trip test and a terminology guard test.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTT0K9RX0004QTE** (completed) — annual calendar; established one week
  per turn, `week`/`year` state, and the `Week W · Year Y` HUD. Direct
  predecessor; this item finishes the vocabulary migration it started.
- **CG-0MTTAOWXN0090724**, **CG-0MTTAOW1S00509OA**, **CG-0MTTAOVLS00056W2**
  (completed) — week-stamping and week-gating follow-ups.
- **CG-0MT53NXGZ004H5AE** — two-turn plan-ahead tutorial flow (source of much
  of the "tomorrow" wording).
- **CG-0MTNMBX5Z002U0MH** — tutorial day-splitting change.
- **CG-0MSXIQIPJ000NDTL** — two-step click-to-place pattern referenced by the
  tutorial ("same-day" → "same-week").

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MRER3RE300418SG** – Income rounding error: fractional baseIncome lost via Math.floor in applyReputationMultiplier (completed)
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed)
- **CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I** – Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right (open)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: day, documentation, duration, need, time (+3 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: day, documentation, duration, need, time (+3 more)
- `README.md` — matched: day, documentation, need, time, turn (+2 more)

## Risks, assumptions, mitigations

- **Save compatibility break (high).** The `'DayStart'` phase value and
  `dayStart*` fields are serialised (`MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`,
  `MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`, schema v1 / campaign v2). *Mitigation:* bump schema
  versions, add an explicit migration, and cover it with a round-trip test
  using a pre-change save fixture (AC 4).
- **Large test churn (medium).** ~45 test files reference `'DayStart'`.
  *Mitigation:* apply a repo-wide rename first, then run unit → dev → full
  test profiles.
- **Over-broad doc edits (medium).** "Everywhere" includes historical PRDs.
  *Mitigation:* terminology-only substitutions; leave legitimate non-turn uses
  of "day" intact (`Day Spa`, `Rainy Day`, `Volunteer Day`, `Farmers Market
  Day`, `St Brigid's Day`, `May Day / Bealtaine`).
- **Ambiguous narrative wording (low).** "overnight" has no week equivalent.
  *Assumption:* use "until next week" (or "by next week"). *Mitigation:*
  reviewer confirms phrasing in the PR.
- **Scope creep (medium).** Rewording unrelated prose. *Mitigation:* record
  extra opportunities as separate work items, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the serialised wire names may change **provided** migration
  preserves old saves; if migration proves riskier than beneficial, keep the
  wire names and rename only in-memory identifiers. This trade-off is left to
  implementation and must be documented in the PR.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 (Surface scope)** — Which surfaces must be standardised: (a) tutorial
text only; (b) tutorial + all other user-facing in-game strings; (c) also
internal code identifiers and comments?
**Answer (producer, in-session reply): `c`** — include internal code
identifiers and comments.

**Q2 (Documentation scope)** — Update only living reference docs, or every
occurrence in every doc, including historical point-in-time documents?
**Answer (producer, in-session reply): `everywhere`** — every occurrence in
every doc.

**Q3 (Canonical wording)** — Confirm the mapping "today"/"this day" → "this
week"; "tomorrow"/"next day" → "next week"; "overnight" → "until next week";
"same-day" → "same-week"; and whether the activity log keeps `Turn N`.
**Answer (producer, in-session reply): `confirmed (stick to Turn N)`** — the
mapping is confirmed and the activity-log label remains `Turn N`.

Prior answers: none (single round of questions). Evidence: producer's
in-session reply; the questions are recorded on the work item as comment
`CG-C0MUDW5CFE004E97Y` ("Intake: blocking questions (needs producer review)").

# Tax Audit should collect 45% of banked coins

## Problem statement

The Main Street Tax Audit incident currently charges a flat 300-coin penalty
(`card-data.csv` row `evt-tax`, `coinDelta = -300`). A flat fee is regressive:
it is trivial for a late-game player with thousands of banked coins and
crippling for an early-game player with a few hundred. The Tax Audit should
instead scale with the player's wealth — collecting **45% of banked coins** —
so the consequence stays meaningful at every stage. Employing the **Accountant**
staff card should soften the blow, reducing the rate to **25%**.

## Users

- **Players** — Want incidents that scale with their economic position so a
  tax audit remains a real setback late-game and is survivable early-game.
- **Players who hire the Accountant** — Want that hiring decision to have a
  tangible, thematic payoff (tax mitigation) in addition to its existing
  market-refresh discount.
- **AI / Monte Carlo balance harness** — Needs the projected cost of the Tax
  Audit (and its Accept/Reject chain evaluation) to reflect the percentage
  mechanic, so simulations stay accurate.
- **TCE developers / producers** — Need a data-driven, testable mechanic that
  extends the existing `EventCard` model without breaking flat-delta events.

### User stories

- "As a player, I want a Tax Audit to take a proportional share of my banked
  coins, so the penalty is fair whether I am rich or poor."
- "As a player, I want hiring the Accountant to reduce my Tax Audit rate from
  45% to 25%, so the staff card feels worth its cost."
- "As an AI player, I want the projected cost of a Tax Audit to use the same
  percentage math as the live game, so my accept/reject decisions are correct."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Percentage collection** — When the Tax Audit (`evt-tax`) incident resolves
   on the Accept path, the coin loss equals **45% of the player's banked coins
   at resolution time** (`state.resourceBank.coins` before the effect).
   *Verification:* unit test seeds a known coin balance, forces `evt-tax`,
   accepts, and asserts the exact resulting balance.
2. **Accountant mitigation** — When the player has the Accountant staff card,
   the Tax Audit rate is **25%** instead of 45%. *Verification:* unit test with
   the Accountant employed asserts a 25% balance delta.
3. **No negative balance** — The coin loss is clamped so `resourceBank.coins`
   never drops below 0 (a tax audit cannot bankrupt a player into negative
   coins). *Verification:* unit test with a low balance asserts the floor at 0.
4. **Pre-existing flat-delta events unchanged** — All other events (including
   the rest of the Tax Escalation chain: `evt-tax-error`, `evt-tax-inquiry`)
   continue to apply their flat `coinDelta` values exactly as before.
   *Verification:* regression test asserting an unchanged flat event's delta.
5. **AI projection parity** — `projectEventCoinDelta()` (used for AI
   affordability/accept-reject decisions) returns the same percentage-based
   magnitude for the Tax Audit as the live resolution path.
   *Verification:* unit test asserting projection equals the applied delta.
6. **Tests** — Unit tests cover percentage resolution, Accountant mitigation,
   zero-balance clamping, flat-event regression, and AI-projection parity.
   *Verification:* targeted `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/`.
7. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
8. **Full suite** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven** — The 45% / 25% rates must be defined as named constants
  (not magic literals scattered through the engine) and referenced from the
  card data or a single config site.
- **Backward compatible** — Existing saves and cards without the new
  percentage field must load and behave exactly as before. The new fields must
  be optional.
- **Deterministic** — The percentage calculation must not consume RNG (it is
  derived from the coin balance), preserving replay/transcript determinism.
- **Chain semantics preserved** — The Accept/Reject dual-choice behaviour of
  the Tax Escalation chain (CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128) is unchanged; only the
  magnitude of the Accept effect changes.
- **Formatting** — The activity-log line for the Tax Audit must show the
  actual coins lost (e.g. "Tax Audit (-225 coins)"), consistent with existing
  `describeEventEffects` output.

## Existing state

- **Tax Audit card**: `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` line 42 —
  `event,evt-tax,Tax Audit,...,All,,-300,0,...,true,,evt-tax-inquiry,,` — flat
  `coinDelta = -300`, `hasChoices = true`, `acceptNextCardId = null`,
  `rejectNextCardId = evt-tax-inquiry`.
- **EventCard model**: `MainStreetCards.ts:385` — `coinDelta: number` and
  `reputationDelta: number` only; no percentage field. `hasChoices`,
  `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId` added by CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128.
- **Event resolution**: `MainStreetEngine.ts` `resolveEvent()` (~line 546)
  applies `state.resourceBank.coins += applyReputationMultiplier(cDelta(event.coinDelta), ...)`
  for `target: 'All'`; staff incident mitigation (`computeIncidentSkillBuffs`)
  already reduces negative incident coin deltas by a percentage.
- **Choice resolution**: `MainStreetEngine.ts` `resolveEventChoice()` (~line 2088)
  calls `resolveEvent()` on Accept and skips it on Reject.
- **AI projection**: `MainStreetEngine.ts:2212` `projectEventCoinDelta()` and
  `eventSeverity()` (~2237) read `event.coinDelta` directly.
- **Accountant card**: `card-data.csv` line 141 — `staff-accountant` with
  `refreshCostDiscount` only (`StaffCard.refreshCostDiscount`,
  `MainStreetCards.ts:557`). "Adds +1 hand slot and makes investment refreshes
  cost 1 less."
- **Difficulty config**: `MainStreetDifficulty.ts` has incident draw pacing
  parameters but no per-event percentage rates.

## Desired change

1. **Card data** — Add an optional percentage field to the event card model
   (e.g. `coinPercentDelta?: number`, value `-0.45` for Tax Audit) and set it
   on `evt-tax` in `card-data.csv` (new column). Update the CSV header and the
   `EventCard` interface/serialisation in `MainStreetCards.ts`.
2. **Engine resolution** — In `resolveEvent()`, when an event carries a
   percentage delta, compute the coin loss from the pre-effect
   `resourceBank.coins`, clamp at 0, and log the actual amount. Flat-delta
   events take the existing path.
3. **Accountant mitigation** — Add a staff-level tax-rate override (e.g.
   `taxAuditRate?: number` / `taxPctDiscount?: number` on `StaffCard`, aggregated
   across `state.staffCards`) so an employed Accountant sets the Tax Audit rate
   to 25%. The engine applies it when resolving the percentage event.
4. **AI projection** — Update `projectEventCoinDelta()` / `eventSeverity()` to
   mirror the percentage math for percentage events.
5. **Tests** — New unit tests for the five verification points in the ACs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Add percentage field/column; set
  Tax Audit to 45%; add Accountant tax-rate field if card-level.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Extend `EventCard` with
  `coinPercentDelta?`; extend `StaffCard` with the tax-rate field; parse from CSV.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `resolveEvent()` percentage
  branch + clamping; `projectEventCoinDelta()` / `eventSeverity()` parity;
  Accountant-rate lookup.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — (only if a typed config field
  is needed for defaults; otherwise untouched).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — Likely home for a
  `computeTaxAuditRate(staffCards)` helper, consistent with existing staff-buff
  helpers.
- `tests/main-street/` — New/updated unit tests (percentage resolution,
  Accountant mitigation, clamping, flat-event regression, AI parity).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — rounding mode is `Math.round`** (standard). The engine already
  uses an integer-rounding helper for fractional effects; the same convention
  is assumed. **OPEN QUESTION Q1** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — no minimum beyond the 0 floor**: the tax can round to 0 for a
  player with very few coins; there is no "always at least 1" rule.
  **OPEN QUESTION Q2** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — scope is Tax Audit only**: the percentage mechanic applies to
  `evt-tax` only; `evt-tax-error` (-200) and `evt-tax-inquiry` (-600) keep
  their flat values (AC4). **OPEN QUESTION Q3** — producer to confirm whether
  the whole Tax Escalation chain should convert.
- **Assumption — Accountant mechanism is a card-level numeric field** (Option A,
  mirroring `refreshCostDiscount`) rather than a new specialization skill.
  **OPEN QUESTION Q4** — producer to confirm.
- **Assumption — rates are difficulty-independent**: 45% / 25% are fixed for
  Easy/Medium/Hard. **OPEN QUESTION Q5** — producer to confirm.
- **Risk — ordering vs `applyReputationMultiplier`**: the percentage must be
  computed from the pre-effect balance, then the reputation multiplier applied
  in the same order as existing deltas. Mitigation: a focused test with
  non-default reputation.
- **Risk — AI/Renderer divergence**: the Tax Audit magnitude appears in the
  engine, the AI projection, and possibly the renderer/animator. Mitigation:
  route all three through one shared helper.
- **Risk — scope creep**: converting the full Tax Escalation chain (and other
  events) is a natural follow-on; recorded as a separate work item if the
  producer wants it, not folded into this change.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128** — Story-driven event chains with dual-choice
  consequences (completed) — defines the Tax Escalation chain and the
  Accept/Reject path that this item's effect feeds into.
- **CG-0MM8RAXJ61L6BG8Z** — Rework event system: reclassify triggers, incident
  queue, investments row, player hand UI (completed) — Tax Audit classified as
  an Incident.
- **CG-0MM8RCFZU03GY009** — Reclassify event triggers and rename Rainy Night
  (completed).
- **CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58** — Content: New chain cards and retro-fitting (open) —
  the Tax Escalation chain source.
- **CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4** — Accountant refresh-discount ability (Group F) —
  the existing Accountant staff buff this change builds alongside.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- **Q1 — Rounding:** When 45% (or 25%) of banked coins produces a fractional
  result, which rounding mode should be used?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used to draft: `Math.round()` (standard), matching the engine's
    existing integer-rounding convention. Recorded on the work item for
    producer confirmation.
- **Q2 — Minimum/Maximum bounds:** Should the tax be floored at 0, floored at
  1 coin, or capped at the total balance?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: clamp the loss so coins never go below 0 (no negative
    balance); no "at least 1" floor.
- **Q3 — Chain cards:** Apply the percentage to Tax Audit only, or to all three
  Tax Escalation cards (`evt-tax-error`, `evt-tax`, `evt-tax-inquiry`)?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: Tax Audit only (per the work-item title); the other two
    keep flat values.
- **Q4 — Accountant mechanism:** How should the 45%→25% reduction be
  represented — a card-level numeric field, a specialization skill, or
  another mechanism?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: card-level numeric field on `StaffCard` (Option A),
    mirroring the existing `refreshCostDiscount` pattern.
- **Q5 — Difficulty scaling:** Are 45% / 25% fixed across Easy/Medium/Hard, or
  difficulty-scaled?
  - Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** — no producer response recorded. Default
    assumption used: fixed across all difficulties.
- **Q6 — Research:** Inspected `card-data.csv` (Tax Audit `evt-tax` row; Tax
  Escalation rows `evt-tax-error`/`evt-tax-inquiry`; `staff-accountant` row),
  `MainStreetCards.ts` (`EventCard`, `StaffCard`, `refreshCostDiscount`),
  `MainStreetEngine.ts` (`resolveEvent`, `resolveEventChoice`,
  `projectEventCoinDelta`, `eventSeverity`), `MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`,
  `MainStreetDifficulty.ts`, and related work item CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128.
  Confirmed: banked coins = `state.resourceBank.coins`; Tax Audit is a
  `target: 'All'` Incident with an Accept/Reject chain; no existing
  percentage-of-balance event effect exists.
data.title: Tax Audit should collect 45% of banked coins

# Save/Load Migration: DayStart → WeekStart

## Summary
Bump the Main Street save schema versions and implement a migration that maps old serialized data (`'DayStart'` phase, `dayStartCoins`, `dayStartRep`, `dayStartScore`) to the new names (`'WeekStart'`, `weekStartCoins`, `weekStartRep`, `weekStartScore`). Existing saves and campaign saves must load without data loss.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Schema versions bumped** — `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` incremented; `MAIN_STREET_CAMPAIGN_SCHEMA_VERSION` incremented.
2. **Migration implemented** — `deserializeWithVersion()` (or equivalent) maps:
   - `'DayStart'` → `'WeekStart'` (phase value)
   - `dayStartCoins` → `weekStartCoins`
   - `dayStartRep` → `weekStartRep`
   - `dayStartScore` → `weekStartScore`
3. **Old saves load** — a save file from the pre-change schema (v1 or campaign v2) loads correctly and produces a valid game state with the new field names.
4. **Campaign saves load** — a campaign save from the pre-change schema loads correctly.
5. **Round-trip test** — a unit test creates a pre-change save, loads it through the migration, serializes it back, and verifies the new schema version and field names.
6. **Transcript compatibility** — transcripts referencing the old phase name can still be replayed (migration applied during load).
7. **No data loss** — all numeric and state values are preserved through migration.

**Key Files:**
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`
- `tests/main-street/` (migration round-trip test)

## Dependencies
`CG-0MUE0L3G80083R0R` (Code Identifier Rename) — the migration maps to the new names produced by the rename.
